elements.label: Figure 1.17
elements.description:
Grouped bar chart with overlaid dots. Y-axis: "Annualized growth rate (%)", scale 0 to 8. X-axis: periods 2010–2012, 2012–2014, 2014–2016, 2016–2018, 2018–2020. Legend: Growth B40 (teal bar), Growth T60 (orange bar), Growth Mean (gray dot). No values are printed; approximate readings are:
- 2010–2012: Growth B40 ~5.4; Growth T60 ~0.6; Growth Mean ~1.4
- 2012–2014: Growth B40 ~4.0; Growth T60 ~2.7; Growth Mean ~2.9
- 2014–2016: Growth B40 ~6.6; Growth T60 ~7.6; Growth Mean ~7.5
- 2016–2018: Growth B40 ~4.9; Growth T60 ~5.6; Growth Mean ~5.5
- 2018–2020: Growth B40 ~4.5; Growth T60 ~6.0; Growth Mean ~5.7
The bottom-40 growth is highest in 2014–2016 and the top-60 growth exceeds bottom-40 growth in every period except 2010–2012, where bottom-40 growth is far higher. Note: Measures based on real household consumption per capita. Source: World Bank staff calculations using VHLSS 2010–2020.

elements.label: Figure 1.18
elements.description:
Bar chart with overlaid dots. Y-axis: "Percent or percentage point", scale -2 to 10. X-axis: country and period labels: 2013–16 China, 2014–18 Indonesia, 2011–18 Mongolia, 2012–16 Malaysia, 2012–15 Philippines, 2014–18 Thailand, 2012–18 Vietnam. Legend: Shared Prosperity (%) (teal bar); Shared Prosperity Premium (percentage point) (orange dot). No values are printed; approximate readings are:
- China: Shared Prosperity ~8.4; Premium ~1.3
- Indonesia: Shared Prosperity ~5.0; Premium ~0.1
- Mongolia: Shared Prosperity ~1.0; Premium ~0.4
- Malaysia: Shared Prosperity ~8.3; Premium ~2.4
- Philippines: Shared Prosperity ~5.1; Premium ~2.5
- Thailand: Shared Prosperity ~1.5; Premium ~0.4
- Vietnam: Shared Prosperity ~4.9; Premium ~-0.1
Vietnam is the only country shown with a negative shared prosperity premium, while China, Malaysia and the Philippines have the highest shared prosperity values. Source: Global database of shared prosperity, seventh edition, World Bank 2020.
